justification: Central claim is an episodic memory loop storing verbal reflections of failed interventions for reuse on later anomalies; ns-3 simulation prototype with an ablation, never run on a live network.

Contribution is a state-machine architecture whose typed agent state and update rules fix what the agent does next across iterations; demonstrated on a lab ocean-model case study, not in operational use.
Argues vector-DB retrieval is the wrong working-memory substrate for agents (no importance flags, no decay, no retrieval-reasoning feedback); a stated position with no method, data or evaluation.
Headline artefacts are hackingBuddyGPT and a new privilege-escalation VM benchmark for measuring autonomous-agent behaviour; all runs are on curated lab VMs, so it is lab validation, not field use.

H-ECA's homeostatic regulation layer computes drives that its executive module turns into the next tactical step; evidence is a lab comparison of two agent instances from an identical baseline, not deployment.

Claim is a deterministic verification layer that gates LLM proposals by P&ID graph traversal before execution (100% recall on injected errors); evaluated on TEP benchmark and synthetic scenarios, not a live plant.
Safety Sidecar uses external verifiers to gate action release and memory writes at runtime; evidence is secure-solution rates across eight CWE scenarios and four LLMs in the lab.

Argues agency requires internalized identity evolution and self-directed learning rather than external scaffolding, proposing the GIC model; a conceptual analysis of agent architectures with no study or measurement.

Contribution is typed persistent state that carries experimental history so the agent stops re-reading it, cutting tokens from O(n) to O(1) per iteration; stateful vs stateless compared on two lab tasks.
Formalizes the Dual-State Action Pair, a guard-function post-condition check that decides whether a generated step may stand; validated on diagnostic probes and SWE-Bench Pro instances in the lab.
AWARE replaces MAPE-K's sequential stage order with an Assess-Weigh-Act-Reflect-Enrich adaptation loop; argued via a comparison to MAPE-K and one demonstration use case, with no measured validation.

Framework turns a human intent into an assembled technology pipeline and re-assembles it on failure, cutting orchestration iterations by ~94%; studied in a cyber-physical testbed, not in factory production.

MCP-SIM's claim is the iterative plan-act-reflect-revise cycle that rewrites failing simulation code after diagnosis; measured across twelve benchmark tasks in the lab against GPT and human-in-the-loop baselines.
ComoRAG's mechanism is a dynamic memory workspace that consolidates probing-query evidence into a global pool across reasoning cycles; evaluated on four long-narrative benchmarks in the lab.

The artefact is an evaluation methodology, a process model plus reference architecture making offline and runtime evaluation a continuous governing function; derived from an MLR and argued, with no validation.

ReAct's contribution is interleaving reasoning traces with actions so the trace induces and updates the action plan; a new prompting technique measured on HotpotQA, Fever, ALFWorld and WebShop in the lab.

An empirical audit of one named mechanism, ReAct's reason-act interleaving, finding performance is driven by exemplar-query similarity instead; evidence is systematic prompt variations run in the lab.
The agent re-attempts the same task by self-correcting after each failure, so the contribution is the revision step; a novel in-context algorithm tested on six text-game tasks in the lab.
RPO's reflector critiques and its optimizer rewrites the agent's action principles from past trajectories between runs, changing the agent itself; a new method measured across four lab environments.

Shows ReAct agents seldom re-evaluate a tool once it enters the thought, and proposes a reflection step that re-checks action safety before execution; evidence is attack/no-attack prompt-injection trials in the lab.

Mechanisms are dual-granularity verification and test augmentation bounding false-admission risk, i.e. what may be accepted as a solution; validated on LiveCodeBench Pro and ICPC-Eval, no real contest use.

The contribution is team composition itself: a language-model graph plus community detection to pick which models collaborate; discovered teams measured against random and hand-curated teams on downstream benchmarks.

Dual-loop reflection updates external latent strategy vectors between interactions so agents evolve stable styles without fine-tuning; evidence is lab runs comparing latent convergence under reflection-driven updates.

P-ReAct restructures reason-act interleaving so tool_call decoding is prioritised and reasoning continues while awaiting tool returns; a new method measured on search-agent benchmarks against LLM agents.

UALA gates whether the agent queries the external world using uncertainty quantification, and reports verbalised confidence is an unreliable signal; measured on HotpotQA, StrategyQA and MMLU in the lab.
